subject: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results

messages.author: 47f3a692f35cc3bf
messages.subject: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
parts:
Dear all,

I am using the VPP_delta model in the hBayesDM package to study addiction individuals. However, there is something strange about the fitting results.

 

I applied this hierarchical Bayesian model to 59 healthy control subjects’ IGT data. The prior distributions of the parameters are shown below. The reason I change the prior distributions is that the markov chains did not converge if the prior distributions are the same as the original settings in the hBayesDM package. Then I randomly split the control group into two subgroups (29 and 30 subjects) and applied VPP_delta model to them respectively. Although the two subgroups were matched according to gender, age and education level, the fitting results showed significant differences between the two subgroups in alpha and lambda. I split the control group into two subgroups randomly again and the fitting results still showed significant differences between the two subgroups. The problem is, the comparison between healthy individuals and patients could be meaningless or unexplainable if we find differences among control subjects.

 

Do you have any idea about this kind of case? Is there something inappropriate about this model that results in this problem?

 

The fitting results are shown below. ‘lambda’ represents the fitting result of ‘lambda’ parameter before I split the control group (59 subjects in total). ‘lambda1’ represents the fitting result of ‘lambda’ parameter of one of the two randomly split subgroups and ‘lambda2’ represents the other subgroup. There are also some other parameters that are different in the two subgroups but mainly alpha and lambda. The fitting results are basically the same when I split the control group into two subgroups randomly again.

 

Looking forward to your reply. Thank you!

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
parts:
Dear Pengyu,

First of all, I do not recommend the use of the VPP model as parameter recovery studies suggest that it is difficult to fully recover the parameters of the VPP model (e.g., Ahn et al., 2014, Frontiers in Psychology). Nate Haines and I came up with an improved model and I believe we will be able to include the model in the hBayesDM package soon. 

When comparing two groups, you need to compare them in a Bayesian way; see https://rpubs.com/CCSL/hBayesDM (4. Compare models (and groups)). i.e., you should not use an independent t-test on posterior means of the two groups. 

Also, if you want to compare randomly-split sub-groups, I believe you need to do it many times (e.g., 100 or 1000) and check how often you observe credible group differences. 

Hope this helps,
Young

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: VPP_delta; something strange about the fitting results
parts:
Hi Dr. Pengyu,


Before answering, I just want to clarify a few points:


1) Do your controls show a large amount of variability in the raw data? If the models are not converging with all 59 subjects, it is possible that there is a lot of variability in response patterns within the control group. This could cause large discrepancies between parameter estimates of each subset.


2) For assessing the difference between parameters of subgroups, what technique are you using? The plot you attached shows what appears to be posterior means of individual subjects, but to compare groups it is important to look at the distribution over the group-level distributions. This can be done with the plotHDI command if you subtract the distributions from each other (e.g., hBayesDM::plotHDI(group1$parVals$mu_lambda - group2$parVals$mu_lambda)). If you are using the means of the posteriors for each subject and not acknowledging the entire posterior (e.g. running a t-test), this will be biased toward showing a difference between groups due to hierarchical shrinkage. 


As for the problems with convergence, what are the problems that you are running into? Are the chains mixing too slowly? Are they getting stuck and not moving at all? Are individual chains sampling from different parts of the parameter space (i.e. multi-modal posteriors)? If you attach a traceplot of your results (e.g., plot(fit, type = "trace")), we may be able to offer more specific advice. 


I hope this helps!


Best,

Nate
